findings.title: mhfe decrypt asks for the BIP39 passphrase where no 24-word reading can come out
findings.reproduction: mhfe decrypt --words 12 on a 24-word container (the `checked` case, one password): the question 'Is a BIP39 passphrase used with the original seed phrase?' and the passphrase prompt come before the work; in script mode with --passphrase-used yes a line is read.
findings.expected: With a stated length of 12 to 21 words the core gives only short readings, which have no 16-bit check, so the passphrase is not asked (HEAD asked only when a 24-word reading came out).
findings.observed: source_check_passphrase asks whenever the container offers the wallet check; tell_source_check prints nothing for the short readings.
findings.impact: A secret is asked and held for nothing, and a script's input line is consumed.
findings.evidence: Source reading by reviewer A; the condition is container.offers_wallet_check() alone.
findings.recommendedFix: Skip the question in the `checked` case, as for one password and a stated short length.
findings.requiredVerification: A terminal case of decrypt --words 12 that goes from the password to the memory reservation with no passphrase question.

findings.title: Under a small locked-memory limit the summary can still reflect that several passwords were typed
findings.reproduction: Linux with `ulimit -l 64`, a 24-word container, about ten extra passwords, then 'Yes' to the passphrase question: the kept Passwords hold locked pages, the passphrase line may fail to lock, and note_unlocked writes its warning on the record. On Windows, the reservation of a larger level made off the record replaces the first level's on-record page-file notice and 'Disk' answer.
findings.expected: The summary is the same for one password or several (AUD-007-SEC005, decrypt.rs:181-182).
findings.observed: The locked-memory warning, and on Windows the page-file notice, can depend on the number or settings of the extra passwords.
findings.impact: A weak signal on the main screen of how many passwords were typed, only under an unusually small limit or on Windows with other settings.
findings.evidence: Source reading by reviewer A, checked by the coordinator against note_unlocked and reserve_largest.
findings.recommendedFix: Ask the 16-bit-check passphrase before add_passwords, and keep the Windows notice of a larger level off the record or say it as for one password.
findings.requiredVerification: A terminal case with a lowered memlock limit comparing the summaries of one and of several passwords.

findings.title: On a Windows console the scroll view and the password headings write secrets through std's stderr
findings.reproduction: Every redraw of the scroll view writes the kept phrase rows and 'Password N: ...' with anstream's eprintln to io::stderr(); on a Windows console std converts each line to UTF-16 in a stack buffer it does not wipe.
findings.expected: Secret lines go through the raw writer that print_phrase uses (raw_io.rs), past std's buffers.
findings.observed: Whole phrases and passwords pass through std's console conversion once per key press.
findings.impact: Unwiped copies on the stack of a Windows process; Unix writes the bytes directly.
findings.evidence: scroll.rs draws kept lines with eprintln!("{line}") (confirmed by the coordinator).
findings.recommendedFix: Write kept lines and password headings through raw_io.
findings.requiredVerification: A Windows terminal run and a code review of every writer of kept lines.

findings.title: An address that two coins share searches their common root twice
findings.reproduction: Compare a non-matching '0x...' address read with Address::parse_any: Ethereum searches 44'/60', then Ethereum Classic 44'/61' and 44'/60' again (coin types [61, 60]); a '1...' address searches 44'/0' for Bitcoin and 145' and 0' for Bitcoin Cash.
findings.expected: At most AddressSearch::addresses() derivations, the scope the screen states.
findings.observed: About 6,000 derivations instead of 4,000 for the default limits, twice that with a passphrase (with it, then without it).
findings.impact: No wrong result; the stated scope understates the work, and the decoy search for two missing words runs about 1.5 times longer than needed.
findings.evidence: Coin types confirmed in src/wallet.rs by the coordinator.
findings.recommendedFix: Skip a root that an earlier coin of the same address form already searched.
findings.requiredVerification: A unit test counting the stopped() calls with SearchLimits::new(1, 1).

findings.title: mhfe check and mhfe rekey disagree on a match of the wallet without the passphrase
findings.reproduction: The same container, password and typed passphrase, and an address of the wallet without a passphrase: check reports 'matches' with 'confirms the phrase, not the passphrase'; rekey refuses with REFERENCE_MISMATCH.
findings.expected: One rule for what a wallet reference confirms, or a check that says rekey needs the wallet with the passphrase.
findings.impact: A rehearsal that matches does not predict a rekey that confirms.
findings.evidence: Source reading by reviewer A; ReferenceMismatch at rehearsal.rs:583 confirmed.
findings.recommendedFix: Decide in the library whether a phrase-only match confirms a rekey, and say it in both front ends.
findings.requiredVerification: Unit tests of both paths with the same reference.

findings.title: The documented check() result shapes are incomplete
findings.reproduction: docs/API.md:836 gives { matches, outcome, path, evidence } without withoutPassphrase; the rustdoc of CheckSession.compare gives JSON without outcome.
findings.expected: Both agree with CheckJson and web/client.d.ts:539-552.
findings.impact: An API reader misses the field that says a match confirmed the phrase only.

findings.title: describeAddress() without a coin does not say which coins it searches
findings.reproduction: describeAddress({ address: '0x...' }) returns { type: null, search: "m/44'/{60,61}'/..." }; a '1...' address returns Bitcoin's 'legacy (BIP44)' type with no mention of Bitcoin Cash.
findings.expected: A page can show the coins searched, as the command line does ('The coins appear as soon as the address is read').
findings.observed: Only coin-type numbers; a page would have to repeat the address-form rule.
findings.impact: Browser front ends cannot name the coins without a second copy of the rule.
findings.recommendedFix: Add coins: string[] (coin ids) to the result, the d.ts and the documents.
findings.requiredVerification: Page checks for '1...', '3...' and '0x...' without a coin.

findings.title: The local tag v0.7.0 names a commit older than what is now documented as 0.7.0
findings.affected: local tag v0.7.0 (0775404, not pushed); docs/releases/v0.7.0.md; docs/releases/unreleased.md:8
findings.reproduction: git rev-parse v0.7.0^{commit} gives 0775404; the working tree documents the removal of mhfe wallets and multi-password decrypt as 0.7.0.
findings.expected: The tag names the commit the notes describe.
findings.observed: Pushing the tag as it is would build 0775404, which still has mhfe wallets and single-password decrypt.
findings.impact: A release of the wrong source.
findings.evidence: git ls-remote shows no v0.7.0 on the remote; no release exists.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-create the unpublished signed tag on the commit that contains these changes.
findings.requiredVerification: git show v0.7.0:src/bin/mhfe/wallets.rs fails, and v0.7.0's notes contain the multi-password entry.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The tag must name the release commit before it is pushed.

findings.title: The README links into files that no release archive carries
findings.affected: README.md (about 25 relative links into docs/ and SECURITY.md); scripts/package-release.sh:98-110
findings.reproduction: add_common_files ships README.md, LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/ only; HEAD's README linked everything else as https://github.com/hobby-eng/mhfe/blob/main/...
findings.expected: A shipped README whose links work offline, or the linked guides in the archive.
findings.observed: In every command-line archive, and as README-mhfe.md in the browser package, the relative links are dead; exit codes, script input, cancellation keys and the security notes are no longer in the archive.
findings.impact: Reference material is missing on the offline computer the archive is meant for.
findings.evidence: Confirmed by the coordinator in scripts/package-release.sh.
findings.recommendedFix: Use absolute GitHub links in the README, or ship docs/CLI.md, docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md and SECURITY.md in every archive.
findings.requiredVerification: A gate that every relative README link resolves to a file the archive carries.

findings.title: The README says the scrollable lines are wiped on exit, which a cancel does not do
findings.reproduction: Ctrl+C or SIGTERM during the recoveries ends the process through restore_and_exit without dropping the kept buffers.
findings.expected: Agreement with SECURITY.md: the handler does not first wipe every buffer; the lines are wiped when the screen closes.
findings.recommendedFix: Say 'wipes them when the screen closes'.

findings.title: decrypt's --stdin help puts the passphrase on a third line, which is wrong with --repair
findings.reproduction: With --repair the input is container, repair words, password, passphrase.
findings.impact: A script written from the help would give its lines in the wrong order.
findings.requiredVerification: A plain case of decrypt --stdin --repair --passphrase-used yes.

findings.title: The v0.7.0 notes have no New section
findings.reproduction: Several passwords in decrypt, dice passwords in the menu, the check of the wallet without the passphrase and the coin told from the address sit under Changed; v0.6.0 has a New section.
findings.expected: Additions apart from changes, as in the earlier notes.
findings.evidence: Comparison of the headings with docs/releases/v0.6.0.md.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a New section and move those entries.

findings.title: 'No' or Escape at the Windows page-file question for a larger memory level is not honoured
findings.reproduction: On Windows, a later password with a higher level whose area is not locked; answer No or Escape at 'Go on although this memory could reach the disk?'.
findings.expected: The command ends, as with one password.
findings.observed: reserve_largest discards the refusal, reserves the first level, and the later password reads 'more memory than this computer could reserve now'.
findings.impact: The person's refusal is overridden and the stated cause is wrong.
findings.evidence: Source reading; `if let Ok` in reserve_largest.
findings.recommendedFix: Fall back only when the reservation itself is refused; pass the person's refusal on.

findings.title: The scroll view counts rows by characters, not terminal cells
findings.reproduction: A password with CJK or emoji characters: its heading takes up to twice the rows counted, and draw overflows the room.
findings.expected: Rows counted in cells, as the line editor does (typed_line::text_cells).
findings.observed: The title and first lines scroll off the alternate screen.
findings.impact: A cosmetic loss of the top lines for wide characters.
findings.recommendedFix: Count with the cell widths the line editor uses.
findings.requiredVerification: A unit test of rows and last_top with a wide-character line.

findings.title: The command line decides hidden-wallet rules apart from the library
findings.reproduction: mhfe decrypt on a 12-word same-length container offers more passwords and the README calls their phrases hidden wallets; ContainerFacts::opens_hidden_wallets() is false there and openHiddenWallets() refuses NO_HIDDEN_WALLETS. On a 24-word container the CLI shows readings that rule I29 refuses in the library.
findings.expected: One source for what a hidden wallet is, or the difference stated as a decision.
findings.observed: The command line shows checked readings (marked Verified or passing) by design; the library and the browser refuse them, and same-length hidden wallets have no known answers.
findings.impact: Two front ends describe hidden wallets differently.
findings.evidence: Source reading; the CLI shows and marks checked readings by design.
findings.recommendedFix: Record the difference as a decision in the library documents, or move the rule into the library and let both front ends follow it.
findings.requiredVerification: Documents and a terminal case on a same-length container.

findings.title: The terminal cases stop before the work of several passwords
findings.reproduction: No case reaches recover_and_show, the 'Not recovered' branch, reserve_largest's fallback, the scroll keys, the summary after a completed recovery with several passwords, or the checked branch.
findings.expected: A case for each claim the documents make, or recorded manual evidence.
findings.observed: The one-password summary is verified only for a run stopped at the memory reservation.
findings.impact: Regressions of the result screen would go unseen by the suite.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a --words 12 terminal case and record a manual run of several passwords with its summary.
findings.requiredVerification: The new case in cargo xtask terminal.

findings.title: One message is built in two places
findings.reproduction: Both build 'An answer is longer than {} bytes; no valid answer is that long.' with different limits.
findings.expected: One function that takes the limit.
findings.recommendedFix: One function with the limit as a parameter.

findings.title: Hand-wrapped comments exceed 100 columns
findings.expected: At most 100 columns; dprint excludes web/ and rustfmt does not wrap comments.
